questions.questionText: Explain the difference between useMemo and useCallback, and when each is actually worth using.
questions.idealAnswer: useMemo memoizes a computed value; useCallback memoizes a function reference. Both take a dependency array and only recompute when deps change. They matter when an expensive computation runs on every render, or when a stable reference is needed to keep memoized children or effect dependencies from re-firing. They are NOT free, so reach for them only after profiling shows a real cost.

questions.questionText: Tell me about a time you had to make a backend change under significant time pressure. How did you balance speed and quality?
questions.idealAnswer: A strong answer uses a concrete STAR situation: the deadline and stakes, the specific tradeoffs made (shipping behind a flag, deferring non-critical refactors, targeted tests on the risky path), how they communicated risk, and the outcome plus what they'd do differently.

questions.questionText: Implement firstNonRepeating(str) that returns the first character that appears exactly once, or null if there is none. Example: firstNonRepeating('aabbc') === 'c'.
questions.idealAnswer: function firstNonRepeating(str){const c=new Map();for(const ch of str)c.set(ch,(c.get(ch)??0)+1);for(const ch of str)if(c.get(ch)===1)return ch;return null;} // O(n) time, two passes.
